messages.subject: Stratified analysis error
parts:
Hi again!

(I made a previous post and tried to delete it to post an updated one but i'm not sure if that worked)

These are the errors i get when trying to run a stratified analysis:

1) after running 'section_the_tree' we get this error message: 

WARNING: Your tree has 77 fossil tips older than 0.6 my!
Make sure that 'fossils_older_than' is set to capture all of the fossil tips in your tree!
(default: fossils_older_than=0.6)

...

Error in if (nodes_to_chainsaw[i] <= numtips) { : 
  missing value where TRUE/FALSE needed

2) Leaving it on the default, i get this error message when running the check command

> check_BioGeoBEARS_run(BioGeoBEARS_run_object)
Read 9 items
Read 158 items

FATAL ERROR: You have time slices, but you do not have 'inputs$tree_sections_list'.
Run 'section_the_tree()' to add tree sections to your input BioGeoBEARS_run_object.


3) When i change the default 'fossils_older_than' settings, the checks come out fine but when i carry on with the runslow command i get this error: 

Error in current_tip_relative_probs_of_each_state[tip_TF, states_to_use_TF] : 
  (subscript) logical subscript too long


Any help will be very greatly appreciated!

Erica

parts:
On Sun, Apr 12, 2015 at 7:58 AM, <ericamiche...@gmail.com> wrote:
Hi again!

(I made a previous post and tried to delete it to post an updated one but i'm not sure if that worked)

These are the errors i get when trying to run a stratified analysis:

1) after running 'section_the_tree' we get this error message: 

WARNING: Your tree has 77 fossil tips older than 0.6 my!
Make sure that 'fossils_older_than' is set to capture all of the fossil tips in your tree!
(default: fossils_older_than=0.6)

Hi,
 
This is a warning, not an error.  So if you actually have 77 fossil tips, then don't change anything and run the script like normal.  If you don't actually have fossils, then you are inputting an incorrect tree -- BioGeoBEARS requires a timetree, you shouldn't just throw in any old non-dated phylogeny.  Please see the "mistakes to not make" page at PhyloWiki.

Cheers, Nick
